## Deferred UI feature (Pip, 2026-07-25) -- ~2 epochs out, dedicated art/dev human to guide

The full 'doom leaking through the windows / weather changing in the sky' environmental-effects vision. Pip's framing: this is 'one jump in overall graphics quality up,' and he expects a dedicated dev/art hire to guide the process, so it is roughly TWO epochs away -- NOT a now item.

### What it becomes
Windows with transparency showing an atmospheric sky/weather layer behind the office that reflects game state (clear -> overcast -> storm -> doom), plus doom-driven environmental effects. The office as a doom-visualizer.

### Foundations being laid now (so this is cheap when it arrives)
- Transparency/overlay compositing POC in the office sandbox v3 (place transparent overlays / posters on walls, stacked, opacity-controlled) -- proves the layering system.
- Doom-glow prototype on cats (sandbox v3) -- proves doom-driven visual effects.
- The state-swap (scummy/decent) in sandbox v2 -- proves state -> visuals.
- BLOCKER dependency: window ART with transparency. Windows are currently a ZERO-promote gap in the asset library; generating window assets (round-2) is the prerequisite.

### Related
Sandbox lineage (office_sandbox), SEED_ART_DIRECTION.md (fidelity split), SEED_ASSET_REGISTRY_AND_VERDICTS.md, the round-2 generation gap-fill (windows/tilesets).

issues.title: Architecture Week: systematic destructive testing + integrity/security review sweep
issues.body:
## Horizon item (Pip, 2026-07-25) -- for Architecture Week / later, not now

Binding future-us into disciplined time. Two workstreams to run SYSTEMATICALLY once we're in an architecture-hardening window:

### 1. Codebase-wide destructive testing
Scale up the adversarial approach that just paid off. Tonight a seeded adversarial UI-state fuzz pass (#886) found a shipping soft-lock (#887) plus a whole antipattern class (#877) that every unit test missed -- because the suite tested function-correctness, not state-invariant robustness under hostile input sequences. Do this deliberately across the WHOLE codebase: invariant + seeded-fuzz coverage for the economy/finance engine, save/load + replay/determinism, event resolution, turn pipeline, and any other stateful subsystem -- not just UI modals. Land durable seeded tests in the non-blocking simulation tier (the #886 pattern).

### 2. Thorough integrity + security review
A proper pass over: input handling, the bug-report/telemetry path, leaderboard board-key + verification/replay integrity (anti-cheat), any file/network IO, dependency surface, and the eventual pdoom-data boundary. Threat-model each; document findings.

### Why now-later
The engine's fundamentals are in place, so these are high-value to do BEFORE the codebase gets much bigger -- but they are a dedicated block, not a scoped-change task. Park here so it's on the horizon.

Proof-of-concept that this works: #886 (adversarial UI-state suite), #877 (the class it surfaced).

issues.title: Modal stacking: no shared LIFO overlay chokepoint (stacked-modal soft-lock)
issues.body:
## Summary
Two independent modal systems (MainUI `active_dialog` for ledger/submenus, and the standalone `bug_report_panel`) don't share a stack. When the Bug Report form is open+focused *underneath* another modal (e.g. the Liability Ledger opened on top of it), the #575 text-focus gate suppresses the top modal's own ESC/L close keys -> the top modal reads as un-closeable (soft-lock). Recovery is 'ESC twice, blind', which is not discoverable.

Found during v0.13.1 play-through (2026-07-25).

## Severity
Edge case (~90% confidence): reachable only when Bug Report is opened FIRST, then the ledger stacked on top. Solo ledger closes fine (two working close paths). A minimal guard (dismiss bug-report when opening the ledger) is being hotpatched onto release/v0.13 as a stopgap.

## Proper fix (this issue)
A real LIFO modal stack / single overlay chokepoint that: (a) registers EVERY modal -- including `bug_report_panel` -- in one LIFO list; (b) closes strictly top-first on ESC/close; (c) routes shortcut input only to the top modal. Belongs on main alongside the carved UI architecture.

## Related
- Side-effect of the #575 text-focus gate fix.
- Distinct from #601 (that is the solo L-to-close, already implemented).
- Symptom overlap only with #600 (F3/dev-tools blocked by the same gate).

Key files: main_ui.gd (active_dialog, _show_ledger_screen, ModalInputBarrier), bug_report_panel.gd, ledger_screen.gd, esc_to_close.gd, keybind_manager.gd (is_text_input_focused gate).

issues.title: test(ui): adversarial modal/overlay lifecycle invariants + seeded fuzz (non-blocking tier)
issues.body:
## What this is

An adversarial "smash it" suite for the interactive UI-state layer: modal / overlay / panel open-close lifecycle and input routing. The existing suite is unit-deterministic and never drives hostile INPUT SEQUENCES against live UI state, so cross-handler desyncs (open dialog A, then B fires mid-flight) were invisible to it. This PR adds a destructive, seeded, fully deterministic GUT suite that boots the real `main.tscn` and tries to break the modal machinery on purpose -- and leaves it in the tree so this whole bug class stays caught.

New file: `godot/tests/unit/simulation/test_adversarial_ui_state.gd` (SIMULATION tier -- non-blocking, so it can be honestly RED without gating the fast lane).

## The invariants it drives (checked after every hostile step)

- **I1** tracked-slot validity: `active_dialog` is null OR a valid, in-tree, visible node
- **I2** no orphan modal panel: every visible top-layer modal panel (z >= 999) IS the tracked `active_dialog`
- **I3** no orphan input barrier: no full-rect MOUSE_FILTER_STOP overlay survives without a tracked owner (a survivor == mouse soft-lock)
- **I4** at most one live barrier after the tree settles
- **I5** button routing integrity: every valid button in `active_dialog_buttons` lives inside the tracked dialog
- **I6** event-presenter consistency: `is_showing_event` <=> an event panel is visible; non-empty queue + idle presenter = stuck
- **I7** closability: after exhausting host close paths, nothing modal remains visible

## Results on this base (main @ 49f46832): 3 GREEN / 7 RED -- all 7 are real bugs of the class

**NEW ship-relevant soft-lock (not the #883 exemplar):** ESC on the staff ID card permanently kills the mouse. `MainUI._input` ESC (main_ui.gd:516) calls `_close_active_submenu()`, which frees ONLY the perks panel; EmployeePanel's full-rect z=998 MOUSE_FILTER_STOP blocker (employee_panel.gd:193-207) is freed only by its own click/close lambdas -- and both lambdas capture the now-freed panel, so the first statement (`perks_panel.queue_free()`) errors on a freed instance and `blocker.queue_free()` is never reached. Solo-reachable in a normal run: hire someone, click the roster entry, press ESC. Caught by `test_every_dialog_kind_opens_and_closes_clean` (I3/I7 on `employee_card`).

The other six RED tests:

1. `test_event_firing_over_each_open_dialog_kind` -- 25 violations: the #883 orphan is NOT ledger-specific; an event firing over ledger / doom-trend / fundraise / financing / staff-card orphans EVERY one of them (visible untracked panel + leaked barrier + unclosable after drain). Root cause main_ui.gd:1787 `_on_event_dialog_opened` (no free of prior occupant). PR #883's free-first guard fixes the panel orphan but NOT the staff-card blocker leak above.
2. `test_orphaned_ledger_amplifies_on_reopen` -- after the orphan, L opens a SECOND ledger: 2 ledger panels on screen at once, orphan never closable.
3. `test_opening_each_dialog_kind_over_a_live_event_dialog` -- the inverse direction: the free-first idiom frees the event PANEL but its click-blocker lives at the viewport root untied to the panel (event_dialog.gd:95-102), so the blocker survives (mouse soft-lock) AND `is_showing_event` sticks true -- all future events queue forever (I6). Reachable today via the dev-overlay jump buttons; any future programmatic open reaches it too.
4. `test_same_frame_collision_event_then_ledger` -- same class, frame-exact (open during `present()`'s await window).
5. `test_rapid_double_open_same_kind` -- double-opening the staff ID card stacks TWO blockers, both unclosable (each new card leaks the prior blocker). Ledger/fundraise double-open is clean (free-first handles it).
6. `test_monkey_full_ops_seeded` -- seed 727272 breaks at step 5; minimal repro trace `["resolve","ledger","resolve","financing","operations","event"]` = open any submenu, event fires, orphan.

GREEN (and must stay green): `test_pairwise_dialog_replacement_matrix` (all 81 ordered pairs of the free-first family replace cleanly), `test_two_queued_events_resolve_sequentially_clean`, `test_monkey_safe_ops_seeded` (140 seeded ops over the free-first family).

## The hostile drivers

- single open/close cycle for every dialog kind (ledger, doom trend, 4 grid submenus, financing, hiring, travel, staff ID card, event)
- the #883 exemplar generalized: an event firing over every open dialog kind
- the inverse: opening each dialog kind over a live event dialog
- same-frame collision (open inside `present()`'s await window)
- full ordered pairwise replacement matrix across the submenu family
- rapid double-open of the same kind
- two queued events resolved sequentially
- orphaned-ledger amplification (L-reopen duplicating the panel)
- seeded monkey fuzz x2 (fixed literal seed `727272`, no Date/Time randomness): SAFE op set (regression lock, GREEN) and FULL op set (documents the class; prints the exact op trace on first violation)

## Gates

- Simulation tier: 106 tests, 7 failures -- ALL 7 are this suite finding the bugs above; the pre-existing 96 sim tests are untouched and green. Suite runtime ~41s.
- Fast gate: GREEN -- 647 tests, 0 failures, 74/74 files (this suite lives in the sim dir, so the fast lane is untouched).

## Expected-red note

The FULL-surface tests are EXPECTED RED until the #877/#883 class of fixes lands (PR #883 is still open, and it only covers part of this). Red here means "the modal layer still desyncs"; every failure prints the seeded op trace that reproduces it. This tier is non-blocking by design.

Related: #877 (LIFO overlay chokepoint), PR #883 (free-first guard -- necessary but not sufficient: it does not fix the staff-card blocker leak or the event-blocker root-parenting).

Do NOT merge without Pip review.

issues.body:
Early-game hiring is a priority to get right (Pip 2026-07-22, playing the A/B build). Two linked gaps:

1. **Onboarding sub-actions as prompts + predictable AP sinks.** Laptop-provisioning + mentoring for a new hire should surface as PROMPTS when a candidate ACCEPTS an offer during the turn, and act as predictable AP sinks you can plan for when you make the offer. Data already exists (researcher fields laptop_done/visa_done/mentoring_done/onboarded) -- it needs surfacing as costed actions.
2. **Interview = schedule -> happen.** Interviewing reads more like SCHEDULING an interview, then it taking place later. When the interview happens, fire a pop-up/notification (pairs with newness-glow, sibling issue).

Gameplay change (AP economy + timing) -> forks the ladder, fine at the 48h mark. Pointers: hiring pipeline, researcher.gd onboarding fields, month_plan/turn_manager (AP), NotificationManager.

issues.title: Character creation and lab setup point allocation system

milestone.title: First Contact
milestone.description: ARC (theme milestone, ~quarterly). Launch-hardening: legibility, onboarding, hotpatches, early-game depth. Spans the v0.13.x..~v0.15 monthly epochs. Nomenclature: docs/RELEASE_NOMENCLATURE.md

issues.body:
## Summary
Add optional character creation where players spend points allocating advantages for lab setup (location, starting funds, reputation, connections, etc.).

## Context
From playtesting session 2025-11-27. Give players agency over their starting conditions while keeping a default for those who want to jump in.

## Features
### Point Buy System
Players get X points to spend on:
- **Location**: Bay Area (expensive, talent pool) vs smaller cities (cheap, less talent)
- **Starting Capital**: More money = less points elsewhere
- **Reputation**: Start with academic credentials vs unknown
- **Network**: Have researcher friends to hire easily
- **Equipment**: Start with compute vs basic laptops
- **Institutional Support**: University affiliation, grants, etc.

### Default Option
- "Start Standard Game" button for players who don't want to optimize
- Balanced default setup

### Presets
- "Academic Spinoff" - university connections, low funds
- "Well-Funded Startup" - VC money, no reputation
- "Solo Researcher" - minimal everything, high autonomy

## Design Considerations
- Keep it simple (5-10 choices max)
- Make trade-offs meaningful
- Replayability: different builds = different experiences
- Balance: no "obviously best" choice

## Priority
Enhancement - adds replayability and player agency

milestone.title: First Contact
milestone.description: ARC (theme milestone, ~quarterly). Launch-hardening: legibility, onboarding, hotpatches, early-game depth. Spans the v0.13.x..~v0.15 monthly epochs. Nomenclature: docs/RELEASE_NOMENCLATURE.md

issues.body:
## Summary
During QA testing, a number of GDScript warnings were observed in the Godot debugger console. These don't cause runtime errors but should be cleaned up for code quality.

## Warnings to address
From the debugger output:

- **Integer division warnings** - Multiple instances of `Integer division. Decimal part will be discarded.`
- **Unused local variables** - Variables declared but never used:
  - `event_type`
  - `start_result`
  - `turn_result`
  - `event_id`
  - `research_label` (shadowing)
  - `current_money`
  - `panel`
- **Ternary operator type mismatch** - `Values of the ternary operator are not mutually compatible`
- **Unused parameter** - `doom_percentage` in `update_doom_level()`
- **Iterator naming conflict** - `seed` iterator has same name as built-in function

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All GDScript warnings resolved or intentionally suppressed with comments
- [ ] No new warnings introduced
- [ ] Game still functions correctly after changes

## Notes
These are style/quality issues only - the game runs fine with these warnings present.
